summary: A Valcour Island light lit in 1874, replaced by a steel tower in 1930, and reached only by boat; its keepers include Mary Herwerth, the widow who kept it.

light.characteristic_note: Current characteristic per Rowlett; LighthouseFriends describes the 1874 fifth-order lens as fixed white

structures.note: Blue limestone tower with octagonal tower on a keeper's house, red-shingled mansard roof (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett)
Steel skeletal tower with automatic light that replaced the manned lighthouse (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett)

access.note: Reached only by boat; island is state land inside the Adirondack Park. Clinton County Historical Association tours Sundays in July and August, 1 to 3 p.m.

visit.note: Rowlett lists the tower open on Sunday afternoons from 1 July to Labor Day

facts.agency: New York State Parks (LighthouseFriends); Adirondack Park Agency (Rowlett); site managed by Clinton County Historical Association

events.note: Light-House Board first proposes a light here, per LighthouseFriends
Title to the site secured in April 1873 (LighthouseFriends; clippings say only 'April')
Tower of blue limestone with keeper's house; roster and Rowlett give 1874
Lit at the opening of navigation in spring 1874, under William C. Wait
Fifth-order Fresnel lens, focal plane 95 ft (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett)
Light-House Board report records a survey of the reservation (item 1004)
Efficiency flags list in the Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1926 (awards for the year 1925) names Thomas Pickup as keeper of Bluff Point, third district
Steel skeletal tower with automatic light replaces the manned lighthouse; station sold to a private owner
Dr. Raboff, a Massachusetts dentist, buys the light station and about 13 acres as a summer residence
NPGallery record dated 26 August 1993 (date published); the sources read give no separate listing date
Light returned to the lantern room of the lighthouse, 16 November 2004; the 1930 skeletal tower had carried the light before this
Restoration begins: LighthouseFriends says August 2014, funded in part by $170,000 from the State of New York; Rowlett says September 2014

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1874 stone lighthouse was the manned light until 1930. The 2004 date Rowlett gives as the deactivation (inactive since 2004) belongs to the 1930 skeletal tower; the light was returned to the lighthouse on 16 November 2004.
LighthouseFriends dates the restoration from August 2014, Rowlett from September 2014; both agree on completion in summer 2016 (Rowlett) and the state's funding. Left as a disagreement in the story.

notes_for_editor: Checked 2026-10-22 against the sources read: LighthouseFriends page (ID 675), USLHS place record (bluff-point), the clippings PDF (RG 26 E 13), the Clinton County Historical Association page, the Rowlett directory entry, the NPGallery asset page (93000873), the Light-House Board report for 1893 (scan p.71, entry 1004 confirmed), the Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1926 (PDF p.18, efficiency flags for 1925 performance, Pickup confirmed) and the Burlington Weekly Free Press, 27 Nov 1902, p.5 (OCR read: 'diseases contracted in the war of the rebellion' attributed to the husband, and 'seriously ill' and 'her daughter' for Mrs. Herwerth). NRHP nomination PDF for 93000873 is not digitised in our cache (placeholder); only the NPGallery asset page was read, so the nomination's own history is absent. NPGallery's 8/26/1993 is the 'Date Published' field, not a listing date; the story says so. The 1902 Burlington paper says the husband died 'some 18 years ago', while LighthouseFriends and the roster date his death to 17 Feb 1881; the story does not use the paper's figure. The OCR of the 1902 paper gives the husband's rank as 'Plain' (probably Captain); the rank is not used. Range: the station record gives range_nm 7.0, while LighthouseFriends says the light could be seen for eighteen miles; unresolved, not used in the story. Keeper roster matched to USLHS by name and position (0.51 km). Ownership is given three ways (NYS Parks in LighthouseFriends, the island owned by New York State in CCHA, Adirondack Park Agency in Rowlett); all three are stated in the story. Restoration start: August 2014 (LighthouseFriends) against September 2014 (Rowlett); both stated. The clippings file is undated and its extracts are not dated individually; the story does not date them. The 1985 'transferred' event was removed because the sources give only 'mid-1980s'. Raboff is named only in his public role (purchaser and offeror) as the published sources give it; the story omits his wife's remarks. Storms, wrecks and rescues: no sourced events for this station, so that chapter is omitted.
